requirements.title: One save model per Rules Engine panel

sources.ref: Workflow measurements: Admin · change a module rule

requirements.requirement: Each Rules Engine sub-tab has exactly one save control that names what it saves and saves only that panel. The header "Save Rules Engine" is removed or shown only on sub-tabs whose content is the parent rules object. All rules panels share one RulesPanelShell (dirty state, Save, Reset, inline status), replacing the seven panel-local feedback variants. Panels that write immediately (Secure Storage) are marked "Saves immediately" and have no Save button.
acceptance: On the Certifications, Equipment, Off-Duty, Agency Training and Fleet sub-tabs no header Save is offered; each panel's own Save persists that panel and a reload shows the saved values.
On Firearms/Range sub-tabs the remaining Save is labelled with its scope and persists only the parent rules (component test).
SV-29 reproduction (change Off-Duty rules, save, reload) shows the change persisted and a visible confirmation.
Every rules panel renders through the shared RulesPanelShell (one feedback style, one Save/Reset layout).
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
Audit writes are unchanged: the same actions write the same audit entries with the same fields as on the baseline (§1b).
requirements.notes: WP-5 (UX remediation plan). SV-29 confirmed live on staging 22e543d. Save semantics (what each endpoint writes) are unchanged; only which button calls which existing endpoint changes.

requirements.title: Settings success notices actually display
requirements.requirement: Success notices after any Settings save remain visible (loadSettings no longer clears the notice in the same batch), including the invite result "added using an existing TracePoint account", which is the admin's only signal that no invitation email was sent.
acceptance: Component test: after saveRules resolves, "Operational rules saved." is in the DOM.
All 14 success sites in settings/page.tsx show their message after the save completes.
The existing-account invite message is visible after invite.
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
requirements.notes: Present in PROD/STG/RC per register-AE. XS fix. Settings save-lifecycle merge (E-04 + E-06 + E-07 + AE-R1).

requirements.title: Background refresh after save keeps the tab mounted
requirements.requirement: Saving does not unmount the active tab into a full-page spinner. The initial load and post-save refresh are separated (refreshing flag); scroll position and context are kept and feedback is shown next to the control that saved.
acceptance: Component test: after a save the active tab keeps the same DOM node and the success notice remains visible.
Scroll position is unchanged after a save on a long tab.
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).

requirements.title: Unsaved-changes guard in Settings
requirements.requirement: A shared useDirtyGuard warns before unsaved edits are lost through tab or sub-tab change, Refresh, navigation or browser unload, and an "Unsaved" pill marks the dirty tab.
acceptance: Edit a Certification rules field, switch sub-tab: a confirmation appears; cancel keeps the edit.
Refresh with a dirty panel asks first.
Unit test: the hook registers beforeunload only while dirty and unregisters when clean.

requirements.title: Range & Qualification rules: one save scope, remove hidden legacy block
requirements.requirement: The qualification cycle cards and the RangeQualificationRulesPanel save through one save scope. The hidden legacy Qualification Standards block and its fetch are deleted.
acceptance: Only one Save control exists on the Range sub-tab and it persists both cycle cards and panel values (reload shows them).
No element with the legacy hidden block renders and its fetch is no longer issued (network log).
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).

requirements.title: Settings tab and section in the URL
requirements.requirement: The active Settings tab and sub-section are read from and written to the URL (?tab=&section=). Existing links that target a section (/settings/fleet → rules, import report "View Users & Roles", shell patch "Open department branding settings") open the intended section.
acceptance: /settings?tab=rules opens the Rules tab; clicking a tab updates the URL with router.replace.
Back/forward and refresh restore the tab.
The three cited links land on the correct tab and section.
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).
requirements.notes: ADM-29 only for the patch-link destination; the patch-link target for non-admins (Home or account) is shell scope.

requirements.title: Settings left rail with search and one home per field
requirements.requirement: Replace the nine overflowing horizontal tabs with the Settings template: a left rail (Agency, People & roles, Policies by module, Integrations; personal settings out) plus a form panel, with a settings filter/search. Each field has exactly one home (agency display name edited in one place, not both "Short display name" and "Agency display name").
acceptance: At 1280px no horizontal tab scroller or white native scrollbar is shown; all nine former tabs are reachable from the rail.
Searching a setting name (e.g. "timeout", "secure storage") lists and opens its section.
The agency display name has exactly one editable control.
Parity inventory for /settings is 100% checked; old ?tab= links redirect to the new sections.
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).
requirements.notes: Blueprint: Settings reorganization is R2/R3 (Stage 4, weeks 9–16). Agency Profile form is the form template to keep (VR).

requirements.title: Usable Settings tab navigation on phones and tablets
requirements.requirement: Below sm the tab bar becomes a select (or the rail collapses to a select), the active tab is scrolled into view, and no white native scrollbar shows on the dark theme.
acceptance: At 375px and 768px every tab and sub-tab is reachable without horizontal page scroll.
The active tab is visible on load.
No light native scrollbar is visible on the tab bar at 768px.
requirements.notes: Superseded by MOD-SET-007 when the left rail ships; keep as the interim fix.

requirements.title: One home per configuration: module policies in Settings with Manage links

sources.ref: Module findings: Settings, Rules Engine & Import
Prioritized usability fixes: One home per configuration

requirements.requirement: Each rule set has one editor in Settings: personally owned rifle program settings, ammunition agency defaults (verification schedules), secure storage locations and fleet rules (Rules → Fleet vs /settings/fleet). Modules link to their settings with a "Manage" link instead of hosting duplicate editors.
acceptance: Rifle program, ammunition defaults, secure storage and fleet rules each have exactly one editable location (parity inventory lists the removed duplicates and their redirects).
/settings/fleet redirects to the Fleet section of Settings.
Values saved in the single editor are what the module uses (same endpoints and payloads as today).
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).
requirements.notes: Blueprint Stage 1 puts "Manage" links from modules in R1; moving the editors is part of the Settings reorganization (R2/R3). The module-side Manage links on Firearms (custody), Personally Owned Rifles and Ammunition belong to the Armory group and should depend on this requirement.

requirements.title: Remove the Dashboard Views tab and orphan dashboard settings route

sources.ref: Prioritized usability fixes: One home per configuration

requirements.requirement: Remove the Settings Dashboard Views tab (it only links back to Customize Dashboard/Analytics) and the orphan /settings/command-dashboard-analytics page; delete or wire the unused AnalyticsDashboardSettingsPanel. The customize entry points on Command Dashboard and Analytics remain.
acceptance: No Dashboard Views tab in Settings; /settings/command-dashboard-analytics redirects to the Command Dashboard customize view.
AnalyticsDashboardSettingsPanel has no dead copy left (deleted or imported and used).
Customize Dashboard and Customize Analytics still save as before.
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).
requirements.notes: OA ADM-30 only for the orphan route (the rest of ADM-30 is repo hygiene, platform scope).

requirements.title: Personal notification preferences live in one place
requirements.requirement: Remove the Settings "My Notifications" tab (or render it with exactly the same props) and link to /notifications preferences, which become addressable (?view=preferences) so the user menu can deep-link to them.
acceptance: Settings shows no second, different version of the preferences panel.
/notifications?view=preferences opens the preferences view directly.
Officers reach their preferences without Settings access (ADM-06 behaviour preserved).
requirements.notes: ADM-06 reachability is already fixed in B11 (see MOD-SET-016). The user-menu link itself is shell scope (blueprint #2).

requirements.title: Security Policy controls state what is enforced (MFA, session timeout, retention)

sources.ref: Module findings: Settings, Rules Engine & Import
Prioritized usability fixes: Honest status copy

requirements.requirement: Every Security Policy row carries an honest state: MFA is shown as "Always required" (disabled switch) in aws-native because the Cognito pool requires TOTP; department session timeout and data retention are badged "Recorded, not yet enforced" until wired; export logging is badged "Enforced". No control implies enforcement that does not exist.
acceptance: In aws-native the MFA switch is disabled and labelled "Always required" (component test).
Session timeout and retention show a "Not enforced" badge until MOD-AUTH-008 ships.
Export logging shows "Enforced".
Copy contains no developer phrasing ("enforcement will be connected as the security layer is completed").
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: hide the unenforced session-timeout/MFA controls or label them (UX plan §8 item 8; OA README §6 ADM-13). Copy-only work; the module owner is deployment per MODULES but the change is presentational.

requirements.title: Audit log: filtered, paginated query with resolved actors; every export audited
requirements.requirement: Provide a server-side audit query filterable by actor, entity, action, record and date with pagination, resolving actor names including platform staff and removed users. The Settings CSV export goes through the audited export endpoint (recordDataExport) with no silent 5,000-row cap.
acceptance: Route test: filters narrow results; pages return stable ordering.
Actor name resolves for a platform admin and for a removed member.
Exporting from the Audit tab writes a data-export audit record.
Audit writes are unchanged: the same actions write the same audit entries with the same fields as on the baseline (§1b).
requirements.notes: OA disposition: Defer (missing capability). OWNER DECISION NEEDED: unaudited CSV exports (security-backlog ADM-12). CSV formula guard already applied by B11 (shared csvCell).

requirements.title: Audit Recent Activity shows names, filters and hides raw IDs
requirements.requirement: Recent Activity shows actor and record names instead of raw UUIDs (IDs behind a copy control), never renders [object Object], and offers the filters the audit query supports. The CSV omits the raw "Changed By User ID" column or pairs it with the name.
acceptance: No raw UUID is visible in the list by default; a copy control reveals it.
Filtering by actor and date returns matching rows.
Help text about audit filters matches what the screen offers.
Audit writes are unchanged: the same actions write the same audit entries with the same fields as on the baseline (§1b).
requirements.notes: Name resolution for current members is possible today; filters and platform/removed actors need MOD-SET-012.

requirements.title: Branding preview does not persist before Save
requirements.requirement: Palette and brightness drafts preview with applyAppearanceToDocument only; persistence happens on Save, the preview reverts on leaving without saving, and the hint copy is corrected.
acceptance: Unit/component test: a draft change does not write tracepoint.appearance.v1; Save does.
Leaving Branding without saving restores the saved appearance.
The hint no longer says "persists for this browser after save" inaccurately.

requirements.title: High contrast becomes a per-user display preference
requirements.requirement: High Contrast is a personal display preference (user menu / personal settings), not an agency-wide setting that changes every user's display.
acceptance: Turning High Contrast on for one user does not change another user's display.
The agency branding section no longer offers High Contrast.
requirements.notes: If per-user server persistence is wanted (across devices), that storage is a track C request to deployment; browser-local storage is acceptable as an interim.

requirements.title: My Notifications reachable by every role
requirements.requirement: Personal notification preferences are reachable by every member (nav "My Notifications" → /notifications hosting NotificationPreferencesPanel), and Help's email-notifications article points there.
acceptance: An officer without Settings permissions opens their preferences without reaching /unauthorized.
Help article route matches the reachable page.
requirements.notes: Fixed by B11 admin correctness (claude/fix-b11-admin-correctness @ b8b3475), merged into the integration branch; UX E-20 confirms it in RC 5b6cc00. Staging step S23 not yet recorded.

requirements.title: Notification delivery schedule copy uses agency time and admin-only notes
requirements.requirement: The Delivery Schedule shows the digest time in the agency's time zone instead of the hard-coded "around 9:00 AM Eastern", and the admin-oriented "New-agency qualification safeguard" note is shown only to administrators.
acceptance: An agency set to America/Chicago sees the digest time in Central time.
An officer does not see the qualification safeguard note.
requirements.notes: Applying the department time zone app-wide (ADM-14) is an owner decision and platform scope; this requirement covers only the panel copy. NotificationPreferencesPanel lives in app/settings/components but renders on /notifications; coordinate with the notifications module.

requirements.title: Digest frequency cards are an accessible radio group
requirements.requirement: Digest choice cards use radio-group semantics (role=radiogroup/radio or native inputs) with visible focus and selected state.
acceptance: axe reports no violation on the digest control.
Screen reader announces the selected option; arrow keys move between options.

requirements.title: Inbox source mutes never hide Critical items
requirements.requirement: Server-side source preferences do not remove Critical inbox items (or the response reports how many items were hidden by source settings), and the source list is derived from the sources the API actually emits.
acceptance: Route test: with source_preferences.Range=false, Critical Range items are still returned.
The response exposes a hidden-count when items are filtered.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: whether Critical inbox items may be muted (UX plan §8 item 7; WP-5). Related A-28 (hard-coded 4 sources) is in the platform group's notifications scope.

requirements.title: Inbox Sources section: own heading, message, placement and hidden-count
requirements.requirement: Inbox Sources has its own heading and save message ("Inbox sources saved", not "Email notification preferences saved"), sits next to its own Save, and the Inbox shows "N items hidden by your source settings — show" when sources are muted. The "Inbox remains the authoritative location" copy is consistent with the muting rule.
acceptance: Component test: saving only sources shows "Inbox sources saved".
The section is not below a Save button that does not apply to it.
With a muted source the Inbox shows the hidden count.
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
requirements.notes: Hidden-count display needs MOD-SET-019; heading/message/placement can ship first.

requirements.title: Remove developer and vendor language from Settings

sources.ref: Prioritized usability fixes: Honest status copy

requirements.requirement: Settings copy contains no developer notes or vendor names: remove "Modules should consume these rules…" and "Loaded permissions: N"; replace the login-email hint with a user workflow ("Contact TracePoint support to change a login email."); align menu labels and page titles ("Settings" vs "Department settings" vs "Admin Settings").
acceptance: grep of settings UI strings finds no "Modules should consume", "Loaded permissions", "Supabase" or "Cognito".
Nav label and page title for Settings match.
The email hint tells the admin what to do.

requirements.title: Accessible dialogs for all Settings modals
requirements.screen: /settings modals (Invite, Edit member, Role permissions, Assign Password)
requirements.requirement: Every Settings modal uses the shared Dialog primitive: role=dialog with label, initial focus, focus trap, Escape to close, inline error slot and busy lock.
acceptance: axe shows no dialog violations; Escape closes; Tab stays within the dialog.
Focus returns to the opener on close.

requirements.title: Settings hint text meets contrast minimum
requirements.requirement: Hint and secondary text use a token at or above slate-400 on the dark surfaces, including placeholders, at no smaller than 12px.
acceptance: No text-slate-600 / placeholder:text-slate-700 remains on slate-900/950 in Settings.
Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for hint text (axe).

requirements.title: Settings touch targets at least 40–44px
requirements.screen: /settings (Notice dismiss, Organization icons, role matrix Edit)
requirements.requirement: The Notice dismiss, Organization icon buttons and role-matrix Edit have a hit area of at least 40px (44px on phone).
acceptance: Measured hit areas ≥ 44px at 375px width for the cited controls.

requirements.title: Agency Profile option lists and honest Configuration Status
requirements.requirement: State, County and Agency type use the same option lists as Create Agency. The always-green "Configuration Status" is relabelled so it does not claim "Live readiness based on saved department data" for checks that are always true.
acceptance: Agency Profile and CreateAgencyForm share the option lists (one constant).
On a new agency with no imported personnel and unreviewed rules, the panel does not show those items as Configured.

requirements.title: Onboarding checklist computed from real agency data
requirements.requirement: Replace the Configuration Status panel with a setup checklist computed from existing data: enabled modules, personnel beyond the admin, pending activations, certification types, qualification standards, rules reviewed, imported records; each item deep-links to where it is done.
acceptance: A new agency shows the incomplete items; completing one (e.g. importing personnel) turns it complete after refresh.
Every checklist item links to the exact Settings section or module page.
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
requirements.notes: OA disposition: Defer (missing capability). If an item has no existing data source it becomes a track C request.

requirements.title: Qualification cycle dates validated
requirements.requirement: Cycle start/end use month/day selects or inline validation instead of free-text MM-DD.
acceptance: Entering 13-40 is impossible or blocked with an inline error before Save.

requirements.title: Secure Storage locations panel: labels, busy state, errors, confirmed deactivate

sources.ref: Workflow measurements: Armorer · set up secure storage

requirements.requirement: Secure Storage is explicitly marked "Saves immediately"; inputs have labels; Save/Deactivate have busy and disabled states (no double submit); network failures show an error; Deactivate uses ConfirmDialog naming the location; a "Show inactive" toggle lists deactivated locations; Edit focuses and highlights the form; Edit/Deactivate are real buttons; copy is consistent; the BOM is removed.
acceptance: Double-clicking Add creates one location (component test).
A rejected save shows an inline error.
Deactivate requires confirmation; cancelling sends no request.
Inactive locations are visible with Show inactive.
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
Audit writes are unchanged: the same actions write the same audit entries with the same fields as on the baseline (§1b).
requirements.notes: Reactivating an inactive location needs an existing API path; if none exists, reactivate is a track C request. Moving secure storage out of policy rules and linking it from custody is covered by MOD-SET-009 and the Armory group's Manage link.

requirements.title: Inert fleet critical-issue toggle shown as locked "Always on"
requirements.requirement: "Critical issues remove vehicles from service" renders as a locked "Always on" row (no switch), and the automatic vehicle status toggle states exactly what it governs (non-critical status derivation).
acceptance: No switch exists for the critical rule; its row reads Always on.
The remaining automation toggle's description names only non-critical behaviour.
Saved fleet rules payload is unchanged (network log).
requirements.notes: Follows F6a (critical holds always apply). FleetRulesPanel is fleet-owned code (Assets & Documents group, FLT-06); this is the Settings screen copy only.

requirements.title: Organization lists: inline rename and labelled deactivate
requirements.requirement: Rename uses an inline edit or modal instead of window.prompt and shows how many members and requirements use the value; Deactivate/Reactivate is a labelled control; the three copy-pasted cards become one OrgListCard.
acceptance: No window.prompt in Organization.
Deactivate shows a text label and accessible name.
Rename dialog shows the affected-member count before Save.
requirements.notes: Affected counts are display-only from existing member data; the cascade itself is MOD-SET-031.

requirements.title: Unit and rank renames propagate to members and scoped requirements
requirements.requirement: Renaming a unit or rank updates members and unit-scoped equipment requirements in one transaction (or members reference unit/title IDs), with an audit entry.
acceptance: Rename "Patrol" → "Patrol Division": members and unit-scoped requirements now match the new name.
One audit record per rename.
Audit writes are unchanged: the same actions write the same audit entries with the same fields as on the baseline (§1b).
requirements.notes: OA disposition: Defer (missing capability).

requirements.title: Invite, member and role errors shown inside the dialog
requirements.screen: /settings → Users & Roles (Invite, Edit member, Role permissions modals)
requirements.requirement: Server errors from the Invite, Edit member and Role permissions modals render in an inline alert inside the open dialog (the modal stays open), not in the page Notice behind the modal backdrop. This includes the deliberate 409 "This person is already a member… Nothing was changed".
acceptance: Component test: invite API returns 409; the dialog shows the message in role=alert and stays open.
Save member and role-permission failures render inside their dialogs.
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
requirements.notes: Listed in the UX plan as a before-production RC-worsened item and in UX-RB §5 as not done. WP-1.

requirements.title: Member Save disabled until groups load; failed load never wipes groups
requirements.requirement: The groups block shows a loading state and Save Access stays disabled until the member's groups have loaded; if loading fails the save omits p_group_ids so existing groups are untouched, and the error copy is not raw database text.
acceptance: Component test: when the groups fetch rejects, Save is disabled or the RPC payload has no p_group_ids.
Opening and saving a member on a slow network never clears their groups.
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
requirements.notes: Present in PROD (non-atomic) and RC (atomic since B11). WP-5.

requirements.title: save_department_member treats absent p_group_ids as no change
requirements.requirement: Confirm (and if necessary make) the atomic member save leave group memberships unchanged when p_group_ids is absent, distinct from an explicit empty list.
acceptance: Route/SQL test: absent p_group_ids keeps existing memberships; [] clears them.
requirements.notes: Verification may show no change is needed; record the test either way.

requirements.title: Invite modal shows one Groups picker
requirements.requirement: The Invite modal renders exactly one "Groups / Assignments" picker (shared GroupChipPicker also used in Edit member), and the duplicate state reset is removed.
acceptance: Component test: the invite modal contains exactly one Groups / Assignments group.

requirements.title: Users & Roles list: search, filters, compact table and overflow actions
requirements.requirement: The member list has search (name, badge, email) and filters (Active / Pending / Inactive, role, unit, activation), sorts, a compact table at lg, and secondary account actions in an overflow menu.
acceptance: In a 150-member seed, typing a name narrows the list to that person.
Status filter Pending shows only pending activations.
Each row has at most one primary action visible; the rest are in the overflow menu.
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).

requirements.title: Dedicated, confirmed "Deactivate member…" action
requirements.requirement: Replace the "Active department membership" toggle saved with routine edits by a danger action "Deactivate member…" with a ConfirmDialog that states the consequences (signs them out and blocks login in this agency) and lists the person's open assignments known to the UI.
acceptance: Component test: deactivation opens a confirmation; cancelling leaves is_active true in the payload.
Confirmation copy is verified against multi-agency behaviour (AE-R2) before release.
The same endpoint and payload are used as today on confirm.
Audit writes are unchanged: the same actions write the same audit entries with the same fields as on the baseline (§1b).
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: copy and policy for the deactivation confirmation (register-AE E-12 "copy and policy decision"). AE-R2: check whether deactivation blocks login for someone still active in another agency before writing "blocks login".

requirements.title: Role permission changes show affected members and a diff before Save
requirements.requirement: Before saving role permissions the dialog shows "affects N members" and a list of added/removed permissions, as a broad-impact ConfirmDialog.
acceptance: Removing a permission shows "−permission" and the member count before Save.
Payload and endpoint unchanged.
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
Audit writes are unchanged: the same actions write the same audit entries with the same fields as on the baseline (§1b).

requirements.title: Rank and unit selects show the stored value even if legacy
requirements.requirement: Rank and Unit selects always include the member's current stored value, labelled "(legacy)" when it is not an active organization item, instead of displaying "Not assigned".
acceptance: A member with rank "Sgt (old)" shows "Sgt (old) (legacy)" selected; an untouched save keeps it.

requirements.title: Invite/Edit hints link to Settings → Organization
requirements.requirement: Hints say "Configured in Settings → Organization" and link there (deep link to the section).
acceptance: Clicking the hint opens Settings → Organization.

requirements.title: One account-action eligibility rule with visible reasons (Settings and Platform)
requirements.requirement: A shared helper decides whether Send Activation, Assign Password and Send Password Reset are enabled for a member (pending, activated, inactive) and why not; the reason is shown as inline helper text (not only a title tooltip), and Settings and Platform use the same confirmation behaviour.
acceptance: Send Password Reset is disabled for inactive members as well as unactivated ones.
The disabled reason is visible as text on phones and to assistive tech.
Settings and Platform Send Activation behave identically (both confirm or neither).
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
requirements.notes: Eligibility mirrors server rules; the server stays authoritative.

requirements.title: Password-reset refusal message without vendor name
requirements.requirement: The 409 refusal returns a stable code and user language ("This account can't receive a reset code yet — resend the activation instead") rather than "Cognito cannot send a reset code…", and does not steer admins to the permanent admin-known password path as the first option.
acceptance: Route test: refusal body has a code and no vendor name; UI renders it beside the row.
requirements.notes: ADM-07b remedy messages were changed on claude/fix-adm07-invited-reset; re-check the RC text against this requirement before starting.

requirements.title: Assign Password dialog: inline error, live checklist, generate/copy
requirements.requirement: Errors appear only in the dialog (onError no longer duplicates them to the hidden page Notice); a live requirement checklist reflects the 14-character policy; generate and copy actions exist; Escape closes; the BOM is removed.
acceptance: Typing a password updates each policy item live.
A server rejection appears once, inside the dialog.

requirements.title: Assign Password warns that self-service recovery depends on a verified email
requirements.requirement: For a pending account the warning and success text tell the admin that the person cannot reset their own password until their email is verified, and recommend Send Activation.
acceptance: Assign Password on a pending member shows the recovery caveat before and after submit.
requirements.notes: Copy must match the outcome of the ADM-07c owner decision (MOD-AUTH-007) and the ADM-07a fix (Assign Password no longer marks email verified without proof).

requirements.title: Member save is one atomic operation
requirements.requirement: Profile fields, roles and groups for a member are saved in one transaction.
acceptance: A role-update failure leaves the member unchanged (no half-update).
requirements.notes: Fixed by B11 (claude/fix-b11-admin-correctness @ b8b3475): save_department_member RPC in aws-native. Bridge-mode member save stays non-atomic (B11 owner decision). Staging step S23 not yet recorded.

requirements.title: Invite works at scale and re-invite never overwrites
requirements.requirement: Invite looks users up directly (no 2,000-user scan), re-inviting is idempotent (no blanking badge/rank/unit or silent reactivation), and an existing member or other-agency identity gets a deliberate 409 rather than a raw 500.
acceptance: Route test: re-invite of an existing member returns 409 "already a member… Nothing was changed".
Invite of an identity from another agency does not return a raw 500.
requirements.notes: Fixed by B11 (claude/fix-b11-admin-correctness @ b8b3475); the 409 now exists (UX E-01 notes it lands behind the modal — see MOD-ADM-001). Staging S23 pending.

requirements.title: Admin APIs return sanitised errors
requirements.screen: Admin API routes (invite, activation, personnel import, super-admin, agency-user-administrator, platform agencies)
requirements.requirement: The admin and platform routes map failures to user messages with a correlation ID and log details server-side; raw database/provider text is not returned.
acceptance: Route test per admin route: a forced database error returns a generic message and correlation ID.
requirements.notes: B11 sanitised the eight admin route files. Residual: about 63 other API routes still pass raw text (security-backlog ADM-32 residual) — platform group (MOD-OPS) scope.

requirements.title: Separation workflow backend: open items, reason, date, checklist
requirements.requirement: Provide an API that lists a member's open firearms, equipment, vehicles, off-duty and personal-rifle requests and remediation items; records separation reason and date; and returns a separation checklist (PDF optional). Asset resolution uses the existing custody operations; login is disabled through the existing Cognito lifecycle.

Edits use the same endpoints as Edit member.

requirements.title: Route tests for invite, import, activation, deactivation, platform and setup

acceptance: CI runs route tests for each listed flow on pull requests.

requirements.title: One honest import capability statement

sources.ref: Module findings: Settings, Rules Engine & Import
Prioritized usability fixes: Honest status copy

requirements.requirement: State import capability once, generated from IMPORT_TYPES: what each importer can commit. Delete the stale "Import Support… preview and validation" card, fix the literal "?" arrow glyphs and give the Import and Exports cards distinct destinations.
acceptance: No screen says personnel/qualification history are preview-only while the wizard imports them.
No literal "?" where an arrow glyph is intended.
The Exports card opens the export section, not the same URL as Import.

requirements.title: One import entry point with a recommended importer
requirements.requirement: One Import page reached from one menu entry; the Settings tab links there. One recommended importer is primary and the others are under "Advanced", with aligned step names and terms across the classic, AI-assisted and multi-file importers.
acceptance: Only one navigation path leads to the import page (the Settings tab is a link; /import redirects).
The recommended path is visually primary; three competing coloured cards are gone.
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).

requirements.title: Split Import / Export / Reports and a stepper beside its steps
requirements.requirement: Import, Export and Reports are separate addressable sections; the step tracker appears only after an importer is chosen, only for importers that use it, and stays sticky next to the step content.
acceptance: Choosing nothing shows no step tracker.
Each section has its own URL; the stepper is visible while scrolling a long step.
Feature parity: same endpoints and payloads before and after, verified in network logs; old URLs keep working or redirect (§4).

requirements.title: Onboarding datasets offer mapping for every importable type
requirements.requirement: Detected Certification and Equipment sheets (and every type in IMPORT_TYPES) offer "Review Mapping" instead of "Mapping support will be added".
acceptance: Component test: a detected Certifications dataset shows Review Mapping.

requirements.title: Classic importer accepts Excel or points to the uploader that does
requirements.requirement: The classic upload accepts XLSX (SheetJS is already a dependency) or clearly points to the Onboarding uploader; the "Excel support can be added after we lock the field mappings" note is removed.
acceptance: Uploading an .xlsx to classic either parses or shows a link to the Excel-capable uploader; no developer note remains.

requirements.title: Mapping cannot silently put employee numbers into Badge
requirements.requirement: Remove "employee number" from the Badge aliases (4 types and dataset detection), prefer exact-alias priority over file order, add an Employee Number field where the target supports it, show sample values per column, and block duplicate source mappings.
acceptance: Unit test of buildAutoMapping: headers [Employee Number, Badge] map badgeNumber → Badge.
Mapping one column to two fields shows a blocking error.
Each mapping row shows sample values.
requirements.notes: Badge is the personnel match key, so a mis-map persists wrong badge numbers. Whether the personnel route accepts an employee-number field is to be confirmed; if not, that is part of MOD-IMP-017.

requirements.title: Import preview: row numbers, errors-only filter, paging, issues CSV
requirements.requirement: Preview shows a row-number column, an "Errors only" filter, paging beyond 25 rows (also when searching), all issues (not first 30), and an issues CSV download.
acceptance: With 120 rows and 40 issues, all 40 are reachable and downloadable and each names its row number.

requirements.title: Personnel import returns created / updated / unchanged per row
requirements.requirement: The personnel onboarding route returns status created | updated | unchanged for each row.
acceptance: Route test: re-importing an existing member returns updated or unchanged, never created.

requirements.title: Import report counts what the server did; confirmation, progress and leave guard
requirements.requirement: Import Records asks for confirmation with the row count, shows N-of-M progress with cancel, guards against leaving mid-import, and the report counts created/updated/unchanged from the server's per-row status instead of counting every personnel row as created.
acceptance: Component test: report counts match server statuses.
Navigating away mid-import asks first.
Save status is server-confirmed: success is shown only after the server confirms the write, and failures are shown in place (§1b).
requirements.notes: Blocked on MOD-IMP-008 for truthful counts; confirmation, progress and beforeunload can ship first.

requirements.title: Import report: totals, +N more, failures CSV, confirmed reset
requirements.requirement: Reviews and failures show totals and "+N more" beyond 50, a CSV of all failures and reviews is downloadable, and Reset / Start New confirm when a report exists.
acceptance: With 120 failures "+70 more" is shown and the CSV contains 120 rows; Reset asks for confirmation.

requirements.title: Report Builder / Export Center: separate errors, human labels, templates for all types
requirements.requirement: Report Builder and Export Center show their own error state; enum options use human labels (shared formatEnumLabel); templates exist for every import type.
acceptance: An export error appears once, in the section that failed; no option shows an underscore value; six templates are offered.

requirements.title: Import pages usable at phone width
requirements.requirement: Below md, import tables become card layouts, nested padding is flattened, and the 7-step grid becomes a "Step N of 7" pill.
acceptance: No horizontal page scroll at 375px on the three import routes.

requirements.title: AI importer: approvals survive non-changing fixes; plain language; honest mode label
requirements.requirement: A fix that does not change counts keeps prior approvals (one summary confirmation instead of four checkboxes); jargon ("decision boundary", "approval fingerprint", "working-state fix(es)", "Minimized samples", "deterministic") is replaced with plain language; the default deterministic mode is labelled honestly rather than implying AI interpretation.
acceptance: Applying a fix that leaves counts unchanged does not reset approvals.
None of the listed jargon strings remain.
Execution still requires the explicit approval the server requires.
Permissions stay server-side: the UI only hides or disables what the server already refuses; no permission logic moves into components (§1b).
requirements.notes: If approval invalidation is enforced server-side (approval fingerprint), keeping approvals needs a server change → raise with deployment before UI work.

requirements.title: Multi-file migration: file names, autosave, confirmed merges, labelled close
requirements.requirement: Resume rows show file names; work autosaves; bulk merges ask for confirmation naming the count; the dialog close button has an aria-label.
acceptance: Bulk merge cancel sends no request; close button has an accessible name; resume list shows file names.
requirements.notes: Undo for merges would need a backend operation (track C) if wanted.

requirements.title: Re-import never strips roles or silently reactivates

acceptance: Route test: re-import of a Sergeant keeps the Supervisor role and active status.
requirements.notes: Fixed by B1a (claude/fix-b1a-reimport-safety @ 6626da7) and F1 (claude/fix-f1-account-import-decisions @ ddcfc58), merged into integration. Staging step S13 not recorded. OWNER DECISION NEEDED (B1a): confirm explicit Active=No deactivates incl. Cognito; aws-native Officer re-add.

requirements.title: Quote-aware CSV parsing and formula-safe CSV writers
requirements.requirement: One RFC-4180 parser keeps line breaks in quoted cells; every CSV writer guards = + - @.
acceptance: A multi-line quoted Notes cell imports into one record; an exported note starting with = is neutralised.
requirements.notes: Fixed by B11 (claude/fix-b11-admin-correctness @ b8b3475); UX E-40 confirms in RC 5b6cc00.

requirements.title: Personnel import without a badge number
requirements.requirement: Badge is optional for personnel import; employee number or email identifies the person (as Invite already allows).
acceptance: A civilian row with no badge imports successfully and matches on email on re-import.
requirements.notes: OA disposition: Defer (missing capability).

requirements.title: Personnel import permission consistent between UI and API

acceptance: The same role is allowed or denied in the UI and every import API.

requirements.title: Cognito personnel import resends Cognito activation, not legacy email

acceptance: Test: importing a previously inactive pending member re-enables them and sends a Cognito invitation without a 500.
requirements.notes: Fixed by B1 (claude/fix-b1-account-access @ 705b540), merged into integration. Staging S1/S13 not recorded.

requirements.title: Reports route gated per report definition

requirements.title: Reports moved out of Import/Export

acceptance: Report output, filters and exports are identical before and after (network log).

requirements.title: Make Administrator: confirmation, feedback, roles column, hidden where meaningless

requirements.title: Invite first administrator from the platform

acceptance: Route test: platform admin invites a chief to an empty agency; the chief has the Administrator role; one audit record.

requirements.title: "Invite first administrator" action on the agency page

requirements.title: Platform Send Activation outside Support Mode

requirements.title: Platform copy: consistent staff and tenant terms, no real-agency placeholders

requirements.requirement: Use one name for platform staff (instead of Super Admin / Platform Admin / TracePoint Platform Administrator / Platform Support / PLATFORM ADMIN) and one for the tenant (agency vs department vs tenant); Create Agency placeholders do not name a real agency; status labels use the shared enum formatter.
acceptance: Glossary terms used consistently across platform screens; no real agency name in placeholders.
requirements.notes: "pilot/pilot" defaults are a provisioning data choice — changing the default values is deployment scope; this requirement covers copy only.

requirements.title: Invited, imported and migrated users can complete first Cognito sign-in
requirements.requirement: The first successful Cognito sign-in of a pending identity activates its link and membership so invited, imported and migrated users reach the app without an admin Assign Password.
acceptance: Staging S1: invite a new user, sign in through Cognito with MFA enrolment, land in the app (not an error or loop).
requirements.notes: Fixed by B1 (claude/fix-b1-account-access @ 705b540). Staging S1 not recorded. OWNER DECISION NEEDED (B1): whether pending users may activate on their first native-app sign-in.

requirements.title: No self-created departments for users without membership
requirements.requirement: create_department_with_owner is not executable by authenticated users; a separated user is told access has ended instead of being offered tenant creation.
acceptance: DB test: an authenticated user with no membership calling create_department_with_owner is denied (E3 db-t5t6t8 reversed).
requirements.notes: Fixed for aws-native by B1 (grant revoked, 039). Bridge (Supabase) /auth/setup path unchanged — relevant only while a Supabase environment is in use.

requirements.title: Settings deactivation disables login and revokes sessions
requirements.screen: Settings member deactivation → Cognito membership lifecycle
requirements.requirement: Deactivating a member in Settings runs the same Cognito disable / global sign-out / session revocation as the import path.
acceptance: Staging S13: a deactivated user's session is rejected and they cannot sign in.
Multi-agency case verified: deactivation in one agency does not wrongly block a member still active in another (AE-R2).
requirements.notes: Fixed by B1 (claude/fix-b1-account-access @ 705b540) together with the 42702 lifecycle bug. AE-R2 multi-agency behaviour not verified in sources.

requirements.title: Application password policy matches the Cognito pool
requirements.requirement: The app and the Cognito pool enforce the same minimum password length so Assign Password never accepts a value Cognito rejects.
acceptance: Test: a password one character below the pool minimum is rejected by the app before calling Cognito (T4 reversed).
requirements.notes: B1 (partial) and F1 set min 14; UX E-54 confirms the modal enforces 14. OWNER DECISION NEEDED: Cognito password minimum — staging CDK 14 vs production hand-patched to 10.

requirements.title: Assign Password no longer marks email verified without proof; clear remedy messages
requirements.requirement: Assign Password does not mark an email verified without proof (ADM-07a), and reset refusals give the admin a correct remedy (ADM-07b).
acceptance: Staging S23-3 (revised) passes.
requirements.notes: Fixed on claude/fix-adm07-invited-reset @ 9a7a234, merged into integration. Staging S23-3 not recorded.

requirements.title: Invited users who have signed in can self-reset their password

acceptance: Staging S23-3 step 2: an invited user who has signed in once receives a reset code.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: ADM-07c remedy after S23-3 (revised) step 2 (defect-stage-ledger).

requirements.title: Department security policy enforcement (session timeout, MFA, retention, export logging)

acceptance: An agency set to 15 minutes is signed out after 15 idle minutes on server and client.
Administrators cannot switch export logging off.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: wire or hide the stored-but-unenforced controls (OA README §6 TRN-07/FLT-06/ADM-13/ADM-14; UX plan §8 item 8). Until decided, the copy requirement MOD-AUTH-001 labels them honestly.

requirements.title: Admin-assigned passwords must be changed at next sign-in

acceptance: A user given a password by an admin is forced to choose a new one at first sign-in.

requirements.title: Sign-in returns the user to the page they asked for
requirements.requirement: The validated `next` destination posted by the login page is stored server-side with the PKCE flow record (internal paths only, via the existing internalAuthRedirect rule) and the callback redirects to it instead of always to `/`. Deep links from notification emails, shared record links, Help and a return after idle sign-out land on the requested record.
acceptance: Route test: begin() with next=/range-days?x=1 followed by a successful callback redirects to /range-days?x=1.
Route test: an external or protocol-relative next (https://evil.example, //evil.example) is ignored and the callback redirects to /.
The `next` value is held in the server-side flow record, never trusted from the callback query string.
Signed out on staging, opening /firearms?x=1 and signing in (including MFA) lands on /firearms?x=1.
Permissions stay server-side: landing on a page the user may not see still returns the normal 403 / unauthorized handling (§1b).
requirements.notes: UX: Source-evident; production has the same cognito-transport.ts begin/callback code (register-AE). V-05 records that the first hop keeps next. Fix together with MOD-AUTH-014 in cognito-transport.ts (register-AE consolidation note). The sign-in part of SV-32; the inbox side-effect part is MOD-OPS-024.

requirements.title: Browser sign-in and sign-out failures redirect to the login page instead of raw JSON
requirements.requirement: For browser (HTML navigation) requests, Cognito endpoint failures (authorization_rejected after a cancelled, expired, replayed or errored flow; authorization_unavailable; logout_unconfirmed; provider_disabled) redirect to `/login?notice=<code>` instead of rendering a JSON document. API and native callers keep the JSON contract.
